chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about standing behind the Imam in the row, what is its limit? He said: 'Standing as much as you can. When you sit and the space becomes narrow, you may move forward or backward, and there is no harm.'

key_terms.إِقَامَةُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ: Standing as much as you can

ai.seo_question: What is the limit for standing behind the Imam in prayer when space is limited?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), this hadith clarifies the practical limits of maintaining one's position in the prayer row (*saff*) when space is constrained. It establishes that the obligation is to remain standing as long as physically possible, but permits minor lateral adjustments—shifting forward or backward—when seated becomes cramped, ensuring the prayer remains valid without requiring the worshipper to break their stance unnecessarily.
